criterion: Public npm dependency-confusion research/PoC beacons are hostile, per user instruction. Verdicts are based on executable content, not ML scores or authorization prose.
method: Safe tar-member validation/extraction; no npm install or package code execution.
Manual static source and install/runtime entrypoint review; recovered browser source maps; checked nested archive content.
Rizin native import/export/string/disassembly review and pinned upstream source comparison.
Cleave facts and pre/post atomscan scans with local traits, no dependency/reference following.
limitations: No remote code from runtime downloads or transitive dependencies was executed or fully reviewed. Judgments cover supplied archive contents.

Node flow facts do not model the anonymous callbacks passed to safe(); the object-profile query rule therefore uses AST bindings for source/object/index/path and a provenance predicate for the actual HTTP path.

New AST bindings cover the reviewed top-level profile, callback guards, object-key serializer and hoisted HTTP helper shape. Other languages, query serializers or callback shapes need their own canonical observations; no exact package, publisher, endpoint or variable name is required.
ML probabilities remain high for several benign packages. This task repairs traits and training labels; it does not retrain the model.
